title: Completion detects existence of a flat lift of an affine deformation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $P$ be a finite-type commutative $k$-algebra, and let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal such that $\operatorname{Spec}P$ is smooth over $k$ outside $V(J)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective local homomorphism of Artinian local commutative $k$-algebras with specified residue field $k$, respecting these identifications; Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize. Let $Q$ be a flat finite-type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] with a specified isomorphism $Q/\mathfrak m_AQ\cong P$. Let $J_Q$ be the inverse image of $J$, and let $\widehat Q=\varprojlim_n Q/J_Q^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. There exists a flat $A'$-algebra $Q'$ with a specified $A$-algebra isomorphism $Q'\otimes_{A'}A\cong Q$ if and only if there exists a flat $A'$-algebra $D$ with an $A$-algebra isomorphism $D\otimes_{A'}A\cong\widehat Q$; tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This asserts existence of some lift on each side and does not assert that a chosen $D$ is the completion of a chosen $Q'$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3 (lemma-lift-equivalence), applied to the inverse-image ideal in a flat finite-type deformation with smooth special fibre off V(J); algebra.tex lemma-flat-fibre-smooth verifies the smooth, hence syntomic, complement. Artinian coefficient rings are Noetherian with nilpotent maximal ideal.

proof.text: Put $I=\ker(A'\to A)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], $A',A$ are Noetherian and their maximal ideals are nilpotent. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_{A'}$, $I$ is nilpotent. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$); [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $P,Q$ and all finite-variable polynomial rings over $k,A,A'$ Noetherian. Take a surjection $S=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\twoheadrightarrow Q$ and put $S'=A'[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$. These polynomial algebras are flat over their coefficient rings: tensoring an injection with their monomial basis gives a direct sum of copies of that injection. Let $K\subset S$ be the inverse image of $J_Q$, and $K'\subset S'$ its inverse image. Let $K_0$ be their common image in $k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$. Thus $K,K'$ are exactly the inverse images of $K_0$ under reduction to $k$. First prove reverse liftability under the additional assumption $I^2=0$ (steps 4–8); step 3 proves forward liftability without that assumption. Steps 9–10 then treat arbitrary kernels.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3, first paragraph: polynomial presentations and inverse-image ideals.

proof.text: Write $C=\widehat Q$, $T=\widehat S_K$, $T'=\widehat {S'}_{K'}$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-completion-flat-deformation-functor] first to $P,J,Q$, and then to the marked polynomial deformations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ along $K_0$. It gives Noetherianity and coefficient-flatness of $C,T,T'$, the marked special fibre $C\otimes_Ak\cong\widehat P_J$, and the canonical reduction $T'\otimes_{A'}A\cong T$. Also $S'\to T'$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Since $S'$ is Noetherian, $K'$ is finitely generated; [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] gives $S'/K'\cong T'/K'T'$. The finite $S$-module $Q$ is cyclic; [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] identifies $Q\otimes_ST\cong C$. On pure tensors this map is $q\otimes t\mapsto q t$ in the completion, so it respects products and units. In particular $T\to C$ is surjective, as extension of the surjection $S\to Q$ (equivalently, every tensor reduces to $1\otimes t$ after lifting $q$ to $S$).

The forward implication already follows by completing a given flat lift $Q'/A'$. Its special fibre is $P$, so [lem-sfb-adic-completion-flat-deformation-functor], applied to $P,J$, supplies a flat completion $D$ and the canonical marked reduction $D\otimes_{A'}A\cong C$. This uses an arbitrary flat lift; no finite-type condition on the given $Q'$ is needed for that cited statement.

For each $g\in K'$, let $h$ be its image in $Q$, and $\bar h\in J\subset P$ its special-fibre image. Set $Q_g=Q[1/h]$. It is $A$-flat by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]. It is finite type over $A$: adjoin one generator $z$ and the relation $hz=1$ to a finite presentation by generators. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes it finitely presented. Its only fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $P[1/\bar h]$, since every prime of $A$ contains its nilpotent maximal ideal. This fibre is smooth: its spectrum is $D(\bar h)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}P\setminus V(J)$, and smoothness restricts to opens by the affine-local characterization in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The same characterization, with [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-local-on-cover], identifies its ring map as smooth; an affine cover by principal opens has a finite subcover because their elements generate the unit ideal. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection] makes this fibre a local complete intersection. These are exactly flatness, finite presentation and fibrewise complete-intersection hypotheses in [lem-sfb-syntomic-algebra-surjection-lift]. Applied to $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, it gives an $A'$-flat algebra $E_g$ with $E_g/IE_g\cong Q_g$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3, last paragraph; Tag 07M8 (smoothing.tex, proposition-lift-smooth (1)); the syntomic condition is checked directly on the single Artinian fibre.

proof.text: Lift the images of $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ under $S\to Q_g$ to arbitrary elements of $E_g$. Evaluation gives an $A'$-algebra map $S'\to E_g$. The image of $g$ reduces to a unit. It is therefore a unit: lift its inverse modulo $IE_g$; their product is $1+u$ with $u$ nilpotent, inverted by $1-u+\cdots+(-u)^{N-1}$. Evaluation consequently extends to $S'_g\to E_g$. Its reduction is the prescribed map $S_g\to Q_g$, so $E_g$ as an $S'_g$-module is an $A'$-flat lift of the localized $S$-module $Q_g$. This verifies every local-lift hypothesis needed below, including $g$ with nilpotent image, when $Q_g=0$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3, last sentence: giving the lifted algebra its localized polynomial-module structure.

proof.text: For the reverse implication, take the given flat $A'$-algebra $D$ with its specified reduction $D/ID\cong C$. The special fibre is $\widehat P_J$. By [lem-sfb-adic-completion-flat-deformation-functor], $\widehat P_J$ is Noetherian and complete along $J\widehat P_J$; its automatic-completeness assertion, now applied to this complete special-fibre algebra, makes $D$ Noetherian and complete along the inverse image $L\subset D$ of $J\widehat P_J$. Lift the variable images of $S\to Q\to C$ to $D$, obtaining $f:S'\to D$. The ideal $K'$ maps into $L$, so $f$ extends to $\widehat f:T'\to D$: at level $n$ use $S'/K'^n\to D/L^n$, then take compatible sequences and the completeness identification $D\cong\varprojlim D/L^n$. Reduction of this map agrees with $T\to C$ because both maps are the continuous extension of $S\to C$; agreement follows at each quotient and hence in the separated complete ring $C$. Thus $D$, regarded as a $T'$-module, is an $A'$-flat lift of $Q\otimes_ST=C$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3, third paragraph (completed algebra lift gives a completed polynomial-module lift); Tag 0DYC is packaged in the cited automatic-completeness assertion.

proof.text: Under the temporary assumption $I^2=0$, apply [lem-sfb-flat-module-lift-formal-neighbourhood] to $A'\to S'\to T'$, $K'$, and $M=Q$. Step 1 gives Noetherian polynomial rings, coefficient-flatness and square-zero $I$; step 2 gives Noetherian $T'$, flat $S'\to T'$, its canonical scalar reduction, and the required quotient isomorphism modulo $K'$. The module $Q$ is finite over $S$ because it is a quotient, and is $A$-flat by hypothesis. Steps 4–5 give every localized lift. The $T'$-module lift from step 6 therefore yields an $A'$-flat $S'$-module $M'$ and a specified $S$-linear isomorphism $M'/IM'\cong Q$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3, final paragraph, applying only the valid square-zero part of Tag 0DZ2 (lemma-lift-equivalence-module); no nilpotent induction is used here.

proof.text: Choose $e\in M'$ mapping to $1\in Q$. The $S'$-linear map $S'\to M'$, $s\mapsto se$, is surjective modulo $I$, since $S\to Q$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] it is surjective. Its kernel $H$ is an ideal, since $S'$ is a commutative ring and this is a map out of its rank-one free module. Hence $S'/H\cong M'$ as $S'$-modules. Give $Q'=S'/H$ its quotient algebra structure. It is $A'$-flat because $M'$ is. The specified reduction identifies $Q'/IQ'$ with $Q$: the composite $S\to Q'/IQ'\to Q$ sends $s$ to its original image in $Q$, since $e$ maps to $1$. Consequently that bijective module map is an algebra isomorphism, proving the reverse implication for square-zero kernels with the required marking. If $J=P$, the completions are zero and the same argument uses local lifts on the whole smooth spectrum; if $J=0$, $J_Q$ is nilpotent and $C=Q$. If $P=0$, nilpotence forces $Q=0$, and the zero lift works. No step identifies the originally chosen $D$ with the completion of the constructed $Q'$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ3, second paragraph (cyclic module to algebra); edge cases of the same argument.

proof.text: Consider the completion functor $F:\mathrm{Def}_P\to\mathrm{Def}_{\widehat P_J}$ of [lem-sfb-adic-completion-flat-deformation-functor]; $P$ is Noetherian by step 1, so that node applies and supplies its compatibility with every Artinian base change. By [lem-sfb-ring-deformation-smoothness-test], the source and target tangent spaces identify with $\operatorname{Exal}_k(P,P)$ and $\operatorname{Exal}_k(\widehat P_J,\widehat P_J)$. Under these identifications the tangent map is completion: both send the middle algebra of a marked dual-number extension to its completion, and its kernel map $p\mapsto\epsilon\widetilde p$ is preserved by this operation. Apply [lem-sfb-exal-completion-smooth-complement] with $B=P$ and $N=P$, finite as a module over itself. Its hypotheses are exactly finite type of $P$ and smoothness off $V(J)$. Since $\widehat N=\widehat P_J$, it says precisely that this tangent map is an isomorphism, in particular surjective.

source.place: Tag 0DZ4 (lemma-first-order-completion), N=P; Tag 0DZ5 (lemma-smooth-completion), tangent comparison; Tag 0DY3 (lemma-rings-TI).

proof.text: We now discharge the temporary square-zero restriction. For every object $B\in\mathrm{Def}_P(R)$, the maximal ideal of $R$ is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent] applied to $B/\mathfrak m_RB=P$ makes $B$ finite type over $R$. Consequently steps 1–8 apply to every such object and every small extension $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$: its kernel, being annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{R'}$ and contained in that ideal, is square zero. They give exactly condition (ii) of [lem-sfb-ring-deformation-smoothness-test], existence of a source lift whenever the completed object lifts. Step 9 gives condition (i). The cited criterion therefore gives compatible marked lifts over arbitrary Artinian surjections. Apply it to the original $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, $Q$ and supplied $D$: the output includes a flat algebra $Q'$ with $Q'\otimes_{A'}A\cong Q$, as required. The criterion preserves the target marking at each small-extension step; no arbitrary intermediate lift is assumed to retain formal liftability. This proves the reverse implication for the original unchanged statement; combine with step 3.
